assertion_analysis.failure_condition: test_a_discarded_request_is_reported_nowhere asserts _stream_file_rows(PROJECT, run_id) == []. It reddens exactly when _report_queued_failure appends a watch-stream row for a run whose discard is recorded, which is the regression the node guards. It is independently sourced — rows written by production code on one side, an empty expectation on the other — and the node's own negative-control.log shows it failing with the discard check removed from _report_queued_failure (FAILED ...::test_a_discarded_request_is_reported_nowhere, EXIT=1, against 4 passed). Not a self-comparison.

test_a_kept_request_is_reported_once_as_queued asserts len(rows) == 1, rows[0]['to_state'] == 'queued' and pointer.get('failure_reported_at'). It reddens if the report stops appending (len 0), appends twice (len 2), lands at the wrong state, or the marker is not stamped — so it guards the over-broad-fix direction the discarded case cannot. It also serves as the positive control for the sibling empty assertion: the same helper sees the one row that is known to be present before the empty result is reported.

findings.text: follow-on: the declared negative control that admits this node was run before the reviewed head's assertion existed. negative-control.log calls _stream_rows(run_id) at its line 148 and its header revision is 86650a11 (working tree, check removed), a helper commit b4e18fe06 deleted; the head asserts through _stream_file_rows(PROJECT, run_id) at tests/test_a_discarded_request_stays_discarded.py:137. The mutation is on production code unchanged since bd4ad8d50 and the same test id reddens, so the guard holds; but the red log is not reproducible from the reviewed revision, and the eight-file arm likewise records no run at b4e18fe06. Does not hold the node.
